title: Ott's Utility Functions
text: otter small collection functions useful , Ott, hopefully others . Sharing caring! Currently otter provides rtf_to_df(), parses RTF files extracts embedded tables data frame. automatically detects header rows, handles multi-page multi-table RTF output, supports non-UTF-8 encodings.

title: Ott's Utility Functions
text: rtf_to_df() reads RTF table returns contents data frame: RTF file contains multiple distinct tables, use table_index select one :
code: library(otter)  path <- system.file("extdata", "example.rtf", package = "otter") rtf_to_df(path, include_header = TRUE) #>    Name Value #> 1 Alice    10 #> 2   Bob    20 multi_path <- system.file("extdata", "multi_table_example.rtf", package = "otter") rtf_to_df(multi_path, include_header = TRUE, table_index = 2L) #>   C D #> 1 3 4

title: Parse an RTF file and extract table body cells into a data frame — rtf_to_df
text: path Character scalar. Path .rtf file. include_header Logical scalar. TRUE, column names taken detected header row. header row auto-detected, first body row used column names dropped data. Default: FALSE header_row Integer scalar. header row use column names include_header = TRUE multiple detected header rows. Defaults last header row. Use 1L first header row. Default: NULL encoding Character scalar. Encoding passed readLines() reading RTF file. Use "latin1" older SAS RTF UTF-8. Default: "UTF-8" table_index Integer scalar. Index table extract RTF contains multiple distinct tables. 1L selects first table, 2L second, etc. NULL merges tables. Default: NULL

title: Parse an RTF file and extract table body cells into a data frame — rtf_to_df
text: data.frame one row per body row one column per cell. values character strings. Column names V1, V2, ... unless include_header = TRUE.

title: Parse an RTF file and extract table body cells into a data frame — rtf_to_df
text: Header rows detected automatically via \trhdr (explicit; Word/SAS) via cell vertical-alignment hints (\clvertalb / \clvertalt) used {r2rtf}. include_header = TRUE header rows auto-detected, first body row promoted column names removed data (analogous read.csv(header = TRUE)). Footnote source rows excluded cell count (span full table width single cell). RTF file contains multiple logically distinct tables (separated paragraph text), use table_index select specific one. default (NULL) merges tables single data frame, correct behaviour paginated single-table outputs.

title: Parse an RTF file and extract table body cells into a data frame — rtf_to_df
code: path <- system.file("extdata", "example.rtf", package = "otter") rtf_to_df(path) #>      V1 V2 #> 1 Alice 10 #> 2   Bob 20 rtf_to_df(path, include_header = TRUE) #>    Name Value #> 1 Alice    10 #> 2   Bob    20  multi_path <- system.file("extdata", "multi_table_example.rtf", package = "otter") rtf_to_df(multi_path, include_header = TRUE, table_index = 2L) #>   C D #> 1 3 4
